name: Channel
listed_description: Thread-safe container for sharing data between threads.
reason: Repo benchmarks/channel_benchmark.cpp (Google Benchmark, GCC 13.3.0, 8-thread CPU, results in a header comment) times only its own queue, vector and array storages against each other (for example 100000-element string inputs: queue_storage 652607002 ns, vector_storage 974087950 ns, array_storage 628774895 ns). No std::thread plus mutex baseline, no other channel library. README and docs make no performance claim.

name: C++React
listed_description: A reactive programming library for C++11.
reason: No numbers against any external baseline. benchmarks/src (Grid, Sequence, Fanout, Random, LifeSim) only compare its own propagation engines. README says it can profile live to decide when parallel updates pay off, with no figures. Wiki page 'Manual updates vs. Signals' is qualitative. Master branch is mid-rewrite; legacy1 README has no benchmark. WebSearch found no third-party comparison.

name: checkedthreads
listed_description: A simple library for (race-checked) parallelism in C and C++.
reason: README only describes performance qualitatively (single shared queue gives optimal load balancing, fast verification via a serial shuffle scheduler). test/sort.cpp prints timings against tbb::parallel_sort when built with TBB, but no results are recorded anywhere reachable, and a WebSearch found only the author's announcement post, which makes no speed comparison.

name: Cinder
listed_description: A community-developed, free and open source library for professional-quality creative coding.
reason: Creative-coding framework (graphics, audio, UI), not a filesystem or I/O library. README has no benchmarks or comparisons with openFrameworks or Processing; WebSearch found only qualitative remarks that it leans on system libraries for speed. libcinder.org was not reachable (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so the github.com repository page was used.

name: ck
listed_description: Concurrency primitives, safe memory reclamation mechanisms and non-blocking data structures.
reason: Directional claims only (ck_epoch 'better than or competitive with many state-of-the-art solutions', 'very fast' spinlocks and sequence locks) with no numbers. regressions/ck_spinlock/benchmark (including pthread.c and linux_spinlock.c), ck_ht/benchmark and others are timing programs whose results are not stored in the repo. The only third-party figure found, a QEMU qht-bench commit message (WebSearch snippet only, page not opened), compares QHT against ck_hs with results behind an imgur link and says ck_hs degrades as writes increase.
